fichas.title: Passage access
fichas.summary: Deck access connects horizontal passages to entrances through internal, projecting, or free-standing vertical structures such as stairs and lifts. Flats may be arranged singly or on two or three sides of a passage. Internal passages can cause single-sided orientation when dwellings occupy one level; arranging dwellings over multiple storeys can improve orientation and enable double-aspect living. External passages run along one long side of a building and are exposed to climatic conditions; subsidiary rooms are generally more suitable beside them. Split-level layouts and alternating passage zones extend the possible arrangements.
uses: Organizing dwellings across one or more storeys

fichas.title: Maisonette with external passage access
fichas.summary: The illustrated residential arrangements show external passage access serving maisonette and split-level dwellings. The text notes that dwelling units extending over two or more storeys, including staggered levels, can support overlapping functions and a wider variety of layouts. Figure 3 shows lower and upper levels; figure 4 shows an external-passage arrangement with living area as referenced in the caption.

fichas.title: Gallery access house with split-level flats
fichas.summary: The gallery-access example depicts split-level flats served by horizontal access passages. The page explains that staggering floor levels by half a storey can support overlapping functions and stratification, while access to every second storey can accommodate larger units on different levels alongside smaller units at entrance level.
